neighbours.label: the agent suffix '-ist' split off as its own piece after a stem (absurd|ist, escap|ist, Gaull|ist)
fire: Her first play was an absurdist comedy about two clocks.
Many readers wanted escapist stories during the war.
The old Gaullist wing of the party opposed the treaty.
Economists described the new tax plan as statist.
The film's colorist gave every night scene a cold blue tint.
As a purist, he refuses to put pineapple on pizza.
The festival showed three absurdist films from Romania.
The game offers an escapist world of castles and dragons.
quiet: Her first play was an absurd comedy about two clocks.
Many readers wanted cheerful stories during the war.
The old conservative wing of the party opposed the treaty.
Economists described the new tax plan as heavy-handed.
The film's editor gave every night scene a cold blue tint.
As a traditionalist chef, he refuses to put pineapple on pizza.
The festival showed three short films from Romania.
The game offers an imaginary world of castles and dragons.

notes: Card: 'ist'/'apist'/'dist' pieces (absurdist, escapist, colorist, statist). Probe: absurdist, escapist, Gaullist, statist, colorist fired; careerist, conformist, Darwinist weak. Near misses use the same stems without '-ist'.
